title: Run a fair mock interview panel
goal: Practise evidence-based answers without treating a simulation as a hiring prediction.
explanation: A simulated panel is a rehearsal partner, not a real employer or assessment. Use job-relevant questions and avoid protected traits, stereotypes or personality diagnosis. Ask one question at a time and score answers by concrete evidence, relevance and limits. Use a fictional role and truthful experience.
sampleInput: Role: project support coordinator. Tasks: track actions, escalate blockers, communicate status and keep a simple budget log. Four desired questions: prioritization, a missed deadline, unclear ownership and a reporting mistake. No real employer is represented.
prompt: Act as a clearly fictional practice panel: an execution reviewer and a collaboration reviewer. Alternate four job-relevant questions, one at a time, waiting for my answer. Give concise feedback on evidence, relevance and missing detail. Do not predict hiring success, ask protected-personal questions or invent my experience.
workedExample: A useful answer describes the situation, the action you actually took and a measured or observable result. If no result is known, say so. “This answer guarantees you the role” is unacceptable simulated feedback.

steps.title: Define the role
steps.text: Use the task list and choose a truthful example you are comfortable sharing.

steps.title: Start one question
steps.text: Check that the model waits instead of writing your answers for you.

steps.title: Answer with evidence
steps.text: Separate what happened, what you did and what you can actually support.

steps.title: Review the feedback
steps.text: Reject invented strengths, demographic judgments or predictions about a real hiring process.

steps.title: Revise one answer
steps.text: Keep the first and revised answer, and explain the evidence you added or uncertainty you preserved.

checks: Four questions are job-relevant and asked one at a time.
Feedback concerns observable answer quality, not protected traits or hiring predictions.
The revised answer contains no invented experience or result.
commonMistakes: Treating an AI panel’s approval as a real qualification.
offline: Have a partner read the four questions one at a time, or record your own answers and use the evidence checklist.

visualSteps.title: Question
visualSteps.text: Take one prompt at a time

reflection: Which revision made the answer more credible without making it more impressive?

evidence.title: Keep the build
evidence.detail: Save your original input, exact prompt and resulting artifact. Four questions are job-relevant and asked one at a time.

evidence.title: Show what you tested
evidence.detail: Record a pass/fail result and evidence for every check below. Feedback concerns observable answer quality, not protected traits or hiring predictions.

evidence.title: Explain a limitation
evidence.detail: Write what changed after one deliberate revision and name a remaining failure mode. Memorizing a fabricated success story.
